examples.label: Children's Services Online Platform (CSSD)
examples.title: Children's Services Online Platform
examples.description:
Implementation of a new Children's Services online platform called Children's Services Online (CSO), offering families a streamlined, accessible way to apply for child care and fee subsidies. 

The new system allows document uploads from home or mobile devices, anytime/anywhere, eliminating the need for in-person visits to City of Ottawa offices.

This flexibility supports families with limited mobility, transportation challenges, or non-traditional work schedules, helping to reduce barriers and increase equity in access to services. An integrated first point of access and simplified application forms make it easier for families, particularly those facing systemic barriers, to complete applications and navigate the system.

examples.label: Human Services Integration Team (CSSD)
examples.title: Human Services Integration Team
examples.description: Human Services Integration Team - Vulnerable residents navigating a social services system face several challenges to their precarious position and limited resources. There are various difficulties that can be nested in limited access of information, complexity of procedures, stigma, discrimination, lack of social supports, transportation, systemic barriers, power imbalance. Identified as a measure under the Term of Council Priorities to simplify access to services, HSI is responsible in the department's adoption of an Integrated Consent Form through training initiatives. The integrated consents are tools that are used in partnership with the client. When signed, the consents allow staff, in collaboration with clients and community agencies, to share information and coordinate services. The consents are legal documents that adhere to privacy laws to ensure the protection of clients' personal information so that relevant information can be shared across programs to facilitate improved access to services.

examples.label: Older Adult Plan Survey Analysis (CSSD)
examples.title: Older Adult Plan Survey Analysis
examples.description:
In Q4 2024, two of our teams collaborated to develop an AI-integrated tool that supported the OAP survey analysis. Here's a high-level overview of what we accomplished:
-        Data Cleanup & Consolidation: We merged data from the Engage Ottawa survey and in-person sessions into a single SharePoint list.
-        AI-Powered Analysis of Open-Ended Responses:
     o   Data Filter: Cleanup of Data, Grammatical corrections and removing any profanities from the ideas received.
    o   Idea Titles: Automatically generated concise  titles for each idea to enable quick scanning.
   o   Keyword Identification: Highlighted predefined keywords within each idea to surface key themes.
   o   Thematic Categorization: Used AI to classify ideas into predefined thematic categories.
-        Dashboard Development:
   o   Created a dashboard for both quantitative and qualitative data analysis to better understand the input and identify priorities.
   o   Developed a stakeholder-facing dashboard to visualize the flow from ideas to priorities, emphasizing accountability and transparency.

examples.label: Point-in-Time Count Online Survey (CSSD)
examples.title: Point-in-Time Count Online Survey
examples.description:
The Nationally coordinated 2024 Point-in-Time count switched from a paper survey collection to an online survey. With the extension of the survey period from 24 hours to five days, going digital provided easier access for 80 different partners to access the survey. Although extending the survey period required increased staff hours dedicated to community response, we coordinated with 311 to respond to inquiries after hours. 

Moving to digital we were able to save the extensive costs of printing over 2800 three-page surveys in addition to the necessary staff hours to complete the subsequent data entry. This streamlined process and will enable faster, more efficient reporting. Also allowed for more collaboration with community partners as was able to provide unique links that will generate agency specific data if requested. Previously, this took 2.5 FTEs 3 weeks to upload into a digital format for analysis.

examples.label: Licensing By-law Review (EPS)
examples.title: Licensing By-law Review
examples.description:
Licensing By-law Review will be brought forward to EPPSC in Q2 2026 - The Council-approved review of the City's Licensing By-law (No. 2002-189) is currently underway. This multi-year project has included a review of existing licensing regulations; processes and public-facing materials; consultation with licensees, business improvement areas and relevant industry groups; and benchmarking licensing regulations and processes in other municipalities. 

Specifically, this review focusses on: modernizing existing licensing regulations and requirements; eliminating duplication and inconsistencies within the by-law and exploring opportunities to reduce red-tape and administrative burdens.

The review also considers non-regulatory issues, such as incorporating technology into the business licensing process and how to better support and inform businesses through both the initial application and license renewal processes

By-law and Regulatory Services is committed to contributing to Council Strategic Objective #21 by implementing  a comprehensive online business licensing platform to streamline and digitalize the end-to-end licensing and permitting process. 

This platform will enable clients to submit applications and payments online, significantly reducing processing times and the need for in-person visits. The system will provide staff with real-time access to application data, support coordination  for required approvals, and improve the ability to track requests from intake through to issuance. 

This comprehensive platform aims to enhance client experience by reducing administrative burden/barriers and streamlining workflows, positioning Ottawa as a top destination for businesses. 

New system is expected to roll out in Q1 2026

examples.label: Budget Literacy and Transparency (FCS)
examples.title: Budget Literacy and Transparency
examples.description:
We continue to undertake a comprehensive consultation and engagement process as part of our annual budget process. The goal of these activities is to offer a wide range of options for residents to be informed and provide input. The resulting feedback ensures transparency and accountability by aligning our budget decisions with community needs and priorities.  

Over this Term of Council, staff have continued to improve and find opportunities to further enhance municipal budget literacy, improve accessibility of budget documentation, provide enhanced reporting in different formats, and emphasize investments towards services and programs that residents rely on and care about the most. Some of these enhancements include:
-	Budget Magazine
-	Budget Explorer
-	Simplified information on Ottawa.ca
-	Budget Document Guide
-	Enhanced social media promotion and electronic advertisement
-	Promotional video on how to have your say!

Based on input from Councillors and the information from Bloomberg Associates, we are pleased to offer the following enhancements as part of Draft Budget 2026:
-	Enhanced Councillor Budget Toolkit
-	Two touchpoints with members of Council, the Mayor, City Manager and Chief Financial Officer to discuss the budget process and priorities
-	Opportunities for Councillor-led public consultations from April to December
-	Simplified budget presentation for ward consultations
-	Continuous improvement of the ward summaries document
-	Earlier public engagement survey 
-	Increased reporting of how resident feedback is considered in the creation of the draft budget
-	New resources to further support budget literacy for residents (ex. graphics, budget pamphlet, FAQ's and promotion of reports that impact the draft budget)

examples.label: Land Management System (PDBS)
examples.title: Land Management System
examples.description: Automation and digital practices - The City is actively applying best practices to optimize and enhance online, self-serve permit application processes for residents and businesses through the implementation of our new digital permit management system called the Land Management Solution (LMS). This new technology solution was introduced in September 2024 and includes a customer portal that allows a user to complete the entire progress online including the ability to fully submit a permit application on any mobile device. This new paperless process allows the building permit applicant to enter information, upload plans and submit payment remotely, without the need to visit a Client Service Centre. Applicants may check on the progress of their application by logging in to their customer portal to view updates and comments from Building Code Services staff and track the status of their application through other service areas forming part of the building permit approval process (such as Development Review & Heritage Planning). Additionally, clients are able to request required inspections from their mobile device and track the status of their applications and permits.

examples.description: Worked with the vendor to design a more robust custom model of waste bin to extend the life of the bins. Sent rusted bins back to the vendor to be refurbished through the warranty. Worked with BIAs and Councillors to ensure we have the right number of bins on street at the right locations - on some streets there was an oversupply of bins and we have been able to reduce the number without reducing the service standards for residents. This is saving the City costs by reducing the total number of assets on street and reducing daily tipping fees for bins that are unnecessary.

examples.label: Plant Your Place Program (PWD)
examples.title: Plant Your Place Program
examples.description:
Through the new Plant Your Place! program, trees are available free of charge to residents through two streams: 1) City-Wide Tree Distribution, and 2) Full-Service Tree Planting in neighbourhoods with low canopy cover. Participants in both program streams will be provided with educational resources and information on tree care and maintenance to support long-term tree health and survival. 

The Plant Your Place! program is a City of Ottawa program delivered in partnership with EnviroCentre. Both program streams support the goals of the City of Ottawa's Urban Forest Management Plan and work towards the vision for Ottawa's urban forest: healthy, diverse, resilient, and always growing.

examples.label: Roads Financial Monthly Reporting Process: (PWD)
examples.title: Roads Financial Monthly Reporting Process:
examples.description:
This initiative involved a monthly financial variance report submitted by the Roads MMS and FSU teams to management to facilitate decision-making. Our team worked collaboratively with the Roads MMS and FSU teams to facilitate a comprehensive purpose alignment and current state mapping session(s) to analyze the process, identify areas for improvement, and establish a clear roadmap for optimizing the workflow. 
Key components of the exercise included: 
- Current state mapping of the process 
- Development and alignment of process vision, mission and individual goals with management priorities and expectations 
- Developing roles and responsibilities 
- Creating RACI charts 
- Identifying opportunities for improvement and streamlining

examples.label: Roads MMS Mobility Project: (PWD)
examples.title: Roads MMS Mobility Project:
examples.description: In its last phase of implementation, the new automated work management process leverages technology (SAP Fiori). It empowers field staff by giving them the technology to stay in the field to complete their paperwork, while providing better, real-time data for analysis. The move to a mobile workforce improves service and reduces the cost of delivering those services. Therefore, we anticipate improved time management, workflow and management reporting, and consistent work management across Roads Services.

examples.label: Sand Screening Project (PWD)
examples.title: Sand Screening Project
examples.description: The Trail Waste Facility and adjoining City-owned properties are made up of a premium sand material.  Solid Waste Services took advantage of this in 2024 by excavating and screening the sand so that it could be used for the current Stage 3B landfill capping project instead of the contractor providing the sand. The City is providing 55,000 cubic metres of sand for the landfill cap. This project has estimated savings of $1.3 million this year.

examples.label: Streamlining Tree Dedication Program (PWD)
examples.title: Streamlining Tree Dedication Program
examples.description: Streamlining processes of former Commemorative Tree Program under the new Tree Dedication Program which now includes spatial data collection for proposed planting locations. The program was expanded to include a wider eligibility for the benefit of residents.  Online payment was not an option previously.  Payment was paid in person or via mailed cheque.  Interacting map with tree dedication will allow user to browse and select a site, when reserving a tree on the interactive map, the application form will pop up to complete. Goal, reduce administrative burden and easier user interface for client.

examples.label: Summer Student Onboarding? (PWD)
examples.title: Summer Student Onboarding?
examples.description: Staff trained on all mandatory courses before commencing field work. Improved safety for summer students and increased productivity to be able to start their full scope of their duties the first week of start date. Worked with H&S, L&D and involved the Sr Clerks in Parks. Increase to almost 100% students completing their mandatory and job specific training on their first 2 days of employment.  This will be implemented throughout PW summer 2025 for all students.  Hoping to eventually be implemented for all new hires.

examples.label: Traffic Infrastructure Mobile Mapping? (PWD)
examples.title: Traffic Infrastructure Mobile Mapping?
examples.description: Traffic Services (Public Works Department) is partnering with the Geospatial Analytical, Technology & Solutions (GATS) branch within the ROW, Heritage & Urban Design Services (Planning, Development, & Building Department) to conduct a comprehensive inventory of traffic assets using the Mosaic Meridian system and Esri Field Maps. This collaboration aligns with GATS' Council-directed mandate to enhance visual and numerical analysis by developing and maintaining the City's Digital Twin, a virtual representation of Ottawa's infrastructure.

examples.label: Winter Maintenance Service Enhancements (PWD)
examples.title: Winter Maintenance Service Enhancements
examples.description: Public Works reviewed the Winter Maintenance Quality Standards to improve winter maintenance of residential roads, sidewalks, cycling pathways, and multi-use pathways for walking, cycling and rollerblading. The Service Delivery review was a comprehensive review of improvements that could be made within the current Winter Maintenance Quality Standards. These improvements resulted in better network conditions through more proactive and aggressive deployment of resources, a redistribution of staff to prioritize sidewalks, and a change to the area boundaries. Winter area boundaries changed to an Urban, Suburban West, Suburban East and a Rural Area structure. The goal for this change was to better align our yards around the type of community and infrastructure they service. This will support development of an urban, suburban, and rural strategy as it relates to event deployment and winter maintenance rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.

examples.label: Winter Parking Availability at City Facilities? (PWD)
examples.title: Winter Parking Availability at City Facilities?
examples.description: Looking at winter parking availability at City facilities and whether it can be expanded during winter parking bans.

examples.label: Parks and Facilities Planning Efficiency Review (RCFS)
examples.title: Parks and Facilities Planning Efficiency Review
examples.description: The Parks and Facilities Planning (PFP) group has begun to implement a series of structural as well as process changes that are streamlining the existing practices. This has involved the development of a new process for the intake and tracking of Cash-in-lieu of Parkland (CIL) funded projects to manage and prioritize Councillor requests.

examples.label: Bus shelter inventory program (TS)
examples.title: Bus shelter inventory program
examples.description:
The scope of the Bus Shelter Inventory Program includes reviewing and streamlining processes for reporting both planned and unplanned changes to the city's bus shelters, ensuring the data remains accurate and up to date. Reliable data enables staff to effectively manage any on-street issues, support the best customer experience, and maintain a strong relationship with the City's bus shelter advertising partner. 

Impact evaluation

examples.label: Departmental cost model (TS)
examples.title: Departmental cost model
examples.description:
The Departmental Cost Model initiative focuses on developing a comprehensive dashboard in collaboration with subject matter experts across the Transit Services and Finance and Corporate Services Department. The model analyzes current expenditures, and key cost drivers across major business lines and serves as a framework to assess the financial impact of future decisions. It is being maintained quarterly to ensure accuracy and relevance, with ongoing enhancements to support improved financial planning and decision-making. 

Outcome monitoring

examples.label: Fleet plan reviews - conventional, Para and non-revenue (TS)
examples.title: Fleet plan reviews - conventional, Para and non-revenue
examples.description:
This initiative supports long-term planning for conventional, para, and non-revenue fleets through tools that use ridership forecasts to determine future capacity needs and guide vehicle purchase schedules through 2048. The proactive approach enables more predictable budgeting, optimizes fleet performance, reduces service disruptions, and supports informed, strategic decision-making over the long term. 

Impact evaluation

examples.label: Investments in the Safety and Security of Ottawa's Transit System - Special Constables Unit (TS)
examples.title: Investments in the Safety and Security of Ottawa's Transit System - Special Constables Unit
examples.description:
As part of its commitment to providing a safe and secure transit system, OC Transpo is making investments within the Special Constables Unit.  Special Constables are sworn peace officers who play an important role in preserving the peace, preventing and investigating crime on transit, protecting customers and employees, and providing assistance to those in need.
Continued investments, in partnership with the Province of Ontario, have allowed OC Transpo to hire 18 additional Special Constables over the last year with more to come in 2026, up to a combined total of 22 new Special Constables over the two-year period.

examples.label: Investments in the Safety and Security of Ottawa's Transit System - Transit Fare Inspectors (TS)
examples.title: Investments in the Safety and Security of Ottawa's Transit System - Transit Fare Inspectors
examples.description: Transit Fare Inspectors were re-introduced to OC Transpo as part of a continuous service improvement initiative. The pilot project was well received and demonstrated the value these positions bring to our transit system.

examples.label: Maintenance dashboards - including bus availability tool (TS)
examples.title: Maintenance dashboards - including bus availability tool
examples.description:
The scope of the Maintenance Dashboard initiative includes developing a Power BI dashboard to display key maintenance-related KPIs. The initial focus is on creating an automated bus availability tool that uses live data to track and visualize daily bus availability over time, comparing it against service planning requirements. The bus availability tool enhances operational visibility, supports data-driven decision-making, and enables timely interventions to improve fleet reliability and service delivery 

Outcome monitoring

examples.label: New Para Transpo Minibuses - Improving Reliability, Safety and Comfort (TS)
examples.title: New Para Transpo Minibuses - Improving Reliability, Safety and Comfort
examples.description:
In 2025, OC Transpo began receiving new seven-metre minibuses for Para Transpo. As part of the renewal of the Para bus fleet, these new minibuses will provide a more reliable, secure and comfortable experience for customers. In total, Para Transpo will receive 76 new seven-metre minibuses, with deliveries between Q1 2025 to Q1 2026.
The new minibus has up to 10 seats, three wheelchair spots, O-Payment readers, and air conditioning. The addition of the O-Payment readers is an important upgrade for customers as it allows them to pay with a credit card, debit card or mobile wallet. For safety, the minibuses are equipped with individual seatbelts, stability belts to secure mobility devices, slip-resistant side and back door ramps, and onboard security cameras.
In addition, Para Transpo has introduced six new six-metre minibuses, which are fully in service as of mid-2025. The new six-metre minibuses are smaller in size but have increased flexibility for maneuvering in urban areas.
As part of the 2026 Budget, On-Demand Transit will be expanded with 10 new seven-metre minibuses. This service will benefit those customers who rely on Para Transpo services.

examples.label: Operator performance Models (absenteeism, on time performance) (TS)
examples.title: Operator performance Models (absenteeism, on time performance)
examples.description:
The Operator Performance Models initiative aims to develop a Power BI dashboard that presents key performance metrics by individual operator and operator groups. The models focus on metrics such as absenteeism and on-time performance (OTP), covering operator groups including Conventional Bus, Electric Rail, Diesel Rail, and Para Transpo Operators. The dashboard supports in identifying trends and conducting spot troubleshooting to enhance service effectiveness and efficiency. 

 

Impact evaluation

examples.label: TOCC Service Performance Dashboard and link with other KPIs (TS)
examples.title: TOCC Service Performance Dashboard and link with other KPIs
examples.description:
The project/initiative is aimed at updating and improving bus and rail service reporting from the Transit Operational Control Centre. This includes performance dashboards as well as streamlining data collection and reporting in order to better support groups such as Customer Service, Engineering, Safety with key performance metrics. The project will include linking measurement and reporting with other KPIs. 


Outcome monitoring
